title: Husqvarna Ear Muffs Hygiene Set: Replacement Cushions
h1: Husqvarna Ear Muffs Hygiene Set
meta: Refresh worn Husqvarna ear muffs with a hygiene set of new ear cushions and foam inserts. Restores seal and comfort for saw, chipper and blower work.
tagline: Replacement cushions and foam inserts that bring tired Husqvarna muffs back to spec.
summary: The hygiene set puts new ear cushions and foam inserts on your Husqvarna ear muffs so they seal and protect the way they did out of the box. Sweat, sawdust and sun break down cushions long before the cups wear out, and a cheap refresh is the fix.
highlights: New ear cushions and inner foam inserts
Restores the seal that sets real-world noise reduction

Quick snap-in swap, no tools
Cheaper than replacing the whole muff

Husqvarna ear muffs, check model compatibility

p: A muff only protects as well as it seals. Once the cushions go hard, crack or flatten, noise from the saw, chipper and stump grinder leaks straight around the cup. Most crews notice it first as a muff that feels loose or that lets the chipper drone through on a long day of feeding brush.

Swap the set as soon as cushions harden or split, and plan on doing it at least yearly if you wear muffs every day. Keep a spare set in the truck so a torn cushion doesn't sideline your hearing protection mid-job.

Husqvarna ear muffs are simple to maintain, which is part of why so many crews run them. The shells and headband last for years if they are not crushed in the truck. The soft parts are the consumables, and the hygiene set is how you replace them without buying a new muff.

Pop the old cushions off the cup rim, pull out the foam, drop in the new foam and press the new cushion on until it seats all the way around. Check that nothing is pinched and that the cups still close flat against each other.
Wipe cushions with mild soap and water, not solvents, and let them dry out of direct sun. For more options see our hearing protection range, including helmet-mounted muffs.

faq.q: How often should I replace the cushions on Husqvarna ear muffs?
faq.a: Replace them whenever they harden, crack or stop sealing, and at least once a year with daily use.

faq.q: Will this set fit any brand of muff?
faq.a: No. It is made for Husqvarna muffs, so confirm your model before ordering.

body.h: Helmet earmuffs on a tree crew
p: Helmet mounted earmuffs solve the biggest hearing protection problem on a job: they never get left in the truck. When the muffs ride on the helmet, the climber has them in the canopy and the ground crew has them at the chipper without thinking about it.

Optime muffs clip into the side slots found on many industrial hard hats and arborist helmets. Check that your helmet takes slot-mount accessories before ordering, and make sure the mount does not interfere with chin straps or face screens.

Adjust the arms so the cups sit centered over your ears with the cushions flat on your head. Hair, safety glasses arms and hoods all break the seal, so keep them out of the way. Replace cushions when they stiffen.

Hearing loss from saws and chippers is permanent and gradual. Wear protection every time an engine is running, and pair muffs with plugs on very loud work like stump grinding. Shop the rest of our arborist helmets and accessories to build a complete setup.

Store the helmet with the muffs in the parked position, not pressed against the shell, so the cushions keep their shape. Swap cushions with a hygiene kit when they harden or crack, and check the mounting arms for cracks after any drop.

faq.q: Will these helmet mounted ear muffs fit my climbing helmet?
faq.a: They fit helmets with standard accessory slots. Many arborist helmets have them, but check your model or its adapter options first.

faq.q: Can I wear them with a face screen?
faq.a: On most slotted helmets, yes. Fit both and confirm the screen and cups clear each other before you head up the tree.

name: Arborist Climbing Helmet
title: Arborist Helmet Guide: Tree Climbing Helmets That Fit
h1: Arborist Helmet and Tree Climbing Helmet Guide
meta: How to choose an arborist helmet: Type 1 vs Type 2, vented vs unvented, chin straps, visors and muffs. A practical guide to tree climbing helmets for crews.
tagline: What to look for in a climbing helmet before you trust your head to it.
summary: An arborist helmet has to stay on through a fall, take a hit from a deadwood stub and still be comfortable after nine hours in the canopy. This page walks through what separates a good tree climbing helmet from a hard hat, and how to pick one for climbing, ground work or both.
highlights: Climbing-style shell with a retention system and chin strap
Accessory slots for face screens and ear muffs
Vented and unvented options for different hazards
Light enough for all-day climbing
Typical price shown is for a mid-range climbing helmet
specs: Climbing, aerial lift and ground work
Slots for face screen and ear muffs (varies by model)
Check each model's labeling for ANSI Z89.1 and EN 12492 / EN 397

body.h: Why a tree helmet is not just a hard hat
p: A standard cap-style hard hat is built to shed a falling object while you stand upright. Climbers spend the day leaning, hanging upside down and swinging into stems. A tree climbing helmet adds a retention system and chin strap so it stays put when your head moves, and a shell shape that protects more of the sides and back.

Look at the labeling, not the marketing. Many arborist helmets carry both an industrial rating (such as ANSI Z89.1 Type 1 or Type 2) and a mountaineering rating. Type 2 helmets are tested for side impacts as well as top impacts, which matters when you can hit a limb from any direction. ANSI Z133 requires head protection on tree work, so pick a helmet that meets the standard your employer or insurer uses.

Weight and balance count too. A light helmet with good ventilation and a low center of gravity is easier on the neck after a full day of climbing and looking up. Try on more than one model if you can; head shapes vary, and a helmet that fits one climber perfectly can create pressure points for another.

Vented helmets are cooler and are the favorite for summer climbing and removals. The trade-off is electrical protection. Vents mean the helmet cannot carry an electrical class rating, so if you work anywhere near conductors, line clearance included, you need an unvented helmet with the right class. Many crews keep one of each.
If you run a mix of climbing and bucket work, an unvented helmet with a good harness is the safer single choice.

Ground crew and bucket operators face many of the same hazards as climbers: falling wood, swinging rigging and low limbs. Many companies now put everyone on site in climbing-style helmets with chin straps rather than cap-style hard hats, so a single model can work across the crew.

Fit decides whether you will actually wear it. Adjust the ratchet so the helmet sits level, a finger width above the brow, and set the chin strap snug enough that the helmet does not rock when you shake your head. Try it with a winter liner if you work in the cold.

Most climbing helmets take a mesh or clear face screen plus clip-in muffs. Add helmet mounted ear muffs and a screen and you have saw protection that never gets left on the truck. Headlamp clips and a light-colored shell help on long summer days.

Check the shell, suspension and chin strap before each use. Replace the helmet after any significant impact, when the shell is cracked, chalky or faded, or when the manufacturer's service life is up. Do not paint the shell or use solvent-based stickers, and keep it out of the dash in direct sun. Climbing in a damaged helmet is not worth the savings.
Keep a record of when each helmet went into service, and mark the date inside the shell. Store helmets in a bag or on a shelf where saws and wedges will not land on them.

faq.q: What is the difference between Type 1 and Type 2 arborist helmets?
faq.a: Type 1 helmets are tested for impacts to the top of the head. Type 2 helmets are also tested for side impacts and penetration, which better matches how climbers get hit.

faq.q: Can I use a vented helmet near power lines?
faq.a: No. Vented helmets do not carry an electrical rating. Use an unvented helmet with the correct electrical class whenever conductors are a hazard.

faq.q: How long does a tree climbing helmet last?
faq.a: Follow the manufacturer's service life, often a few years from first use, and replace it immediately after a hard impact or visible damage.

name: 18 in. Drop Zone Cone
title: 18 in. Drop Zone Cones for Tree Work Sites
h1: Drop Zone Cones, 18 in.
meta: Mark the work zone under the climber with 18 in. drop zone cones. Bright, stackable and easy to set out so the ground crew and public stay clear of falls.
tagline: An 18-inch cone that tells everyone on site where not to stand.
summary: Drop zone cones mark the area under a climber or aerial lift where cut wood, tools and debris can land. An 18 in. cone is tall enough to see over brush and short enough to stack a handful behind the seat of the truck.
highlights: 18 in. height, easy to spot on lawns and pavement
High-visibility orange body
Stacks for compact storage
Weighted base resists tipping on uneven ground
Use with signs and flaggers for roadside jobs

p: Every climb and every bucket job has a drop zone: the ground where cut pieces, deadwood, dropped tools and rigging can come down. It is bigger than most people think. Pieces bounce, roll on slopes and kick off limbs on the way down. ANSI Z133 expects the crew to establish and control that area, and cones are the simplest way to make it visible.

Set the cones before the first cut, not after someone wanders under the tree. A ring of four to eight cones around the drip line, extended downhill and in the direction of any lowering, gives the ground crew a clear boundary and tells homeowners and passersby where they cannot go.
Drop zone cones also protect the climber. A ground worker who is not where the climber expects is the reason many cuts get paused or rushed, and a clear boundary takes that guesswork out of the job.

Cones only work if the crew respects them. Agree on simple commands between climber and ground: nobody enters the zone until the climber gives the all clear, and the climber stops cutting when someone calls in. Keep the chipper, trucks and brush piles outside the cones where you can.
Move cones as the job moves. When you rig a big limb out over a driveway, the landing area may be well past the original ring. Re-set cones for each phase so the marked zone matches the real one.

Brief the client before work starts. Homeowners often want to watch, and pets and kids wander. Show them the cones, explain that the area inside is off limits until the crew says otherwise, and ask them to keep animals indoors.

On jobs along a street or sidewalk, drop zone cones are part of a bigger setup. You may also need advance warning signs like a tree work ahead sign, channelizing devices and flaggers, depending on local rules and the traffic control plan for the road. Smaller 18 in. cones are good for marking the work area itself, but check what your jurisdiction requires for lane closures, which often calls for taller cones or drums.
Ground crew working near traffic should wear high-visibility apparel so drivers see people, not just cones.
At the end of the day, pick up every cone. Cones left behind on a street or lawn become a hazard of their own and are an easy way to lose a set.

Hose off sap and mud so the color stays bright, and replace cones that are crushed, faded or missing reflective collars if your set has them. Stack them in a corner of the truck bed with a strap so they do not blow out on the highway.
A set of cones is cheap, so replace them before they look tired. Faded, dirty cones blend into the background and stop doing their job.

faq.q: How many drop zone cones do I need?
faq.a: Most residential jobs use four to eight cones to ring the work area. Larger removals and roadside work need more.

faq.q: Are 18 in. cones enough for lane closures?
faq.a: Often not. Many jurisdictions require taller cones or drums for road work, so check the traffic control rules for your area.

faq.q: How big should the drop zone be?
faq.a: Large enough to contain anything that can fall, bounce or roll, including rigged pieces. Extend it downhill and in the lowering direction.

name: 48 in. Tree Work Ahead Sign
title: 48 in. Tree Work Ahead Sign for Roadside Jobs
h1: 48 in. Tree Work Ahead Sign
meta: A 48 in. tree work ahead sign warns drivers before they reach your crew. Roll-up design packs small on the truck; pair it with a stand for roadside jobs.
tagline: Advance warning for drivers so your crew has room to work along the road.
summary: A tree work ahead sign gives drivers advance notice that a crew, chipper and falling brush are around the next bend. The 48 in. size is the common full-size format for roadside advance warning.
highlights: 48 in. diamond, full-size advance warning
Bold TREE WORK AHEAD legend
Roll-up style packs flat in the truck
Use with a sign stand for roadside setups
Pairs with cones and flaggers

p: Drivers need time to slow down and move over before they see a chipper in the lane. A tree work ahead sign placed well ahead of the work area does that job. How far ahead depends on road speed and local rules, so follow the traffic control plan for the road you are on, which in the US is usually based on the MUTCD.

If you are buying a tree work ahead sign with stand, choose a stand rated for the sign size and wind, and use the legs on soft shoulders. Weight the base, never with rocks or loose material that can become a hazard.
Check the sign face for scratches, fading and dirt before each job. A sign that cannot be read at speed is not doing its job, and many jurisdictions expect signs to meet reflectivity requirements.

The sign is the first thing drivers see. After it come channelizing devices, a taper and the work area itself, marked with drop zone cones around the tree. Crew on the ground should wear high-visibility vests. Take signs down or cover them when the crew leaves so drivers keep trusting them.
Plan where the sign goes before the truck arrives, especially on busy roads. Setting signs from the far side of the truck keeps the crew out of traffic while they work.

faq.q: Where should I place a tree work ahead sign?
faq.a: Ahead of the work area at a distance set by road speed and local traffic control rules. Check your state or city requirements.

faq.q: Does the sign come with a stand?
faq.a: Check the listing. Roll-up signs are often sold separately from the stand.

name: Hi-Viz Green Mesh Safety Vest, Class 2, XL
title: Green Construction Vest: Hi-Viz Mesh Class 2, XL
h1: Hi-Viz Green Construction Vest, Mesh Class 2
meta: A breathable green construction vest in hi viz green mesh with reflective stripes. Class 2 visibility for ground crew working near roads, chippers and trucks.
tagline: Breathable hi viz green mesh vest so drivers and operators see your ground crew.
summary: This green construction vest keeps ground crew visible around traffic, trucks and loaders without trapping heat. The open mesh breathes on hot days of dragging brush, and the reflective stripes pick up headlights early and late.
highlights: Fluorescent yellow-green mesh body
Reflective striping front and back
Labeled Class 2
Breathable mesh for summer brush work
Size XL fits over a work shirt or light jacket

body.h: Who needs a vest on a tree job
p: Anyone on the ground near a road, a driveway with traffic, or moving equipment should be easy to spot. High viz green is the most visible color against brush, grass and gray pavement, and a Class 2 vest adds enough background and reflective material for most roadside tree work.
Flaggers and anyone working right next to fast traffic may need a higher class. Follow the traffic control plan and your employer's rules.
Mesh vests are the summer choice. When the crew is dragging brush and feeding the chipper on a hot day, a solid vest gets pulled off within the hour. A breathable vest stays on, which is the point.

Loose clothing and the chipper infeed do not mix. Wear the vest closed and snug, keep it zipped or fastened, and replace any vest with torn panels or dangling straps. A breakaway style is a good choice for crew who feed the chipper often.
Wash on gentle and line dry to keep the color and stripes bright. Faded vests lose their visibility. Combine it with drop zone cones and signs for a complete work zone.
Choose a size that fits over the clothes you actually wear. An XL vest over a light jacket fits most adults, but a vest that is too large flaps and can snag on brush.

faq.q: Is hi viz green better than orange?
faq.a: Both are approved high-visibility colors. Fluorescent yellow-green tends to stand out better against green vegetation and in low light.

faq.q: Is a Class 2 vest enough for roadside work?
faq.a: It is common for many road jobs, but some sites and speeds require Class 3. Check your traffic control plan.

h1: Clogger Chaps: Zero Light and Cool, Apron Style
meta: Clogger chaps in the Zero Light and Cool apron style: lightweight, breathable leg protection for ground sawyers who buck and limb all day in the heat.
tagline: Light, cool apron-style chaps for sawyers who spend all day on the ground.
summary: Clogger chaps in the Zero Light and Cool apron style are built for ground work in hot weather, where heavy chaps get left in the truck. The apron cut wraps the front of the legs and buckles on fast over work pants.
highlights: Apron style buckles on over your own pants
Lightweight, breathable build for hot-weather bucking
Cut-protective layers across the front of the legs
UL certified, per the product name
Quick to put on and take off between saw tasks

body.h: Why sawyers choose Clogger chainsaw chaps
p: Most leg cuts happen on the ground, bucking and limbing, when the saw is low and you are tired. The best chaps are the ones you actually wear, and Clogger built the Zero line around comfort so they stay on all day, even in summer heat.
Apron chaps protect the front of the legs, where nearly all saw contact happens. They clip around the waist and legs and come off fast when you switch to dragging brush or running the chipper.

The Light and Cool version is aimed at warm-weather crews. Lighter outer fabric and a breathable build mean less heat trapped against the legs while you are bent over a log, so you are less tempted to leave them off for a quick cut.

Chaps should cover from the waist to at least two inches below the top of the boot. Pick the length that does that for you. Wash per the label; oil and sawdust buildup can reduce performance, and any cut through the outer shell means the chaps need replacing.
Chaps are a last line of defense, not a substitute for training and good saw handling. Climbers who need protection in the tree should look at Clogger Zero chainsaw pants instead.

faq.q: Can I climb in Clogger chaps?
faq.a: Apron chaps are meant for ground work. Climbers are better off in chainsaw pants that move with a saddle.

faq.q: When should chainsaw chaps be replaced?
faq.a: After any cut through the outer layer, or when they are worn, torn or heavily contaminated with oil.

name: Endless Loop Polyester Round Sling, Blue
title: Endless Sling: Blue Polyester Round Sling for Crane Picks
h1: Blue Endless Sling, Polyester Round Sling
meta: A blue polyester endless sling for crane picks and heavy tree rigging. Round sling construction protects bark and cut faces; capacity is on the tag.
tagline: Heavy-duty blue round sling for crane-assisted removals and big picks.
summary: An endless sling made from polyester round sling construction is the go-to choke for crane-assisted tree removals. The soft, circular sling wraps the stem, grips without crushing and spreads load across a wide area.
highlights: Endless round sling, usable in vertical, choker or basket hitch
Polyester core yarns inside a protective cover
Blue color code for quick capacity ID on the ground
Soft on bark and cut faces
Rated capacities printed on the sewn tag
specs: See sewn tag for vertical, choker and basket ratings

p: When the crane is on site, the endless sling is what connects the pick to the hook. Choked around the stem above the balance point, it grips the wood evenly and does not bite into it like chain or wire rope. Two slings let the climber set a balanced pick on long leaders.

Round slings are color coded so the crew can pick the right capacity at a glance. On blue endless sling capacity, the common industry color code puts blue well into heavy-pick territory, but the only number that counts is the one on the sewn tag, and choker hitch capacity is lower than vertical.
The endless design means there is no fixed eye to wear out. Rotate the contact point between picks so the same area of the sling does not always take the bend around the stem or the hook.

Inspect every circular sling before use. Pull it from service if the tag is missing or unreadable, the cover is cut or melted, core yarns are showing, or it has been exposed to heat or chemicals. Pad it on sharp edges, including fresh cut faces and hardware.
Only trained, qualified crews should rig crane picks, working to the crane operator's plan and ANSI Z133. For lighter rigging in the tree, see our crane slings range.

faq.q: What is the capacity of a blue endless sling?
faq.a: Blue sits high in the standard round sling color code, but always use the vertical, choker and basket ratings printed on the sewn tag.

faq.q: Can I use an endless sling as a choker on a stem?
faq.a: Yes. Choker hitch capacity is lower than vertical, so check the tag and protect the sling from sharp edges.

name: Husqvarna K770 Power Cutter
title: Husqvarna K770 Power Cutter: Specs, Price & Uses
h1: Husqvarna K770 Power Cutter
meta: The Husqvarna K770 power cutter: a 74 cc cut-off saw for concrete, pavers, pipe and steel. Specs, typical price, blade options and jobsite tips for crews.
tagline: A proven 74 cc cut-off saw for concrete, pavers, pipe and steel on the jobsite.
summary: The Husqvarna K770 is a gas power cutter that takes 12 in. or 14 in. blades and handles concrete, masonry, pipe and metal. Tree and landscape crews keep one on the truck for curb cuts, paver work, root barrier trenches and cutting steel cable and hardware.
highlights: 73.5 cc two-stroke engine
Takes 12 in. or 14 in. blades
Active air filtration for dusty cutting
Wet cutting kit for dust control
Reversible cutting arm for cutting close to walls and curbs
specs: about 22 lb (14 in., without fuel and blade)

body.h: What the K770 does on a tree and landscape crew
p: The Husqvarna K770 is not a tree tool, but plenty of tree and landscape companies end up owning one. Removals near hardscape lead to curb and sidewalk cuts. Root work turns into cutting a trench for a root barrier through compacted soil and old concrete. Stump jobs uncover buried pipe, rebar and steel cable. A power cutter turns each of those into a quick cut instead of an afternoon with a sledge.
K770 Husqvarna owners like it because it is simple. The engine starts easily, the cutter is balanced for its size, and parts and blades are easy to find. It is a common rental-yard saw for a reason.

The K770 also earns its place on storm work, where uprooted trees tear up driveways, fences and utility hardware. Being able to cut a broken slab, a bent post or a steel guard out of the way gets the tree crew working sooner.

The K770 runs a 73.5 cc two-stroke engine rated at about 5 horsepower. Fit a 14 in. blade for close to 5 in. of cutting depth, or a 12 in. blade for lighter handling. Use the right blade for the material: diamond blades for concrete and masonry, abrasive or metal-rated diamond for steel and ductile iron. Never mount a blade rated for a lower RPM than the saw.

The cutting arm can be reversed so the blade sits on the outside, letting you cut closer to walls and curbs. The air filtration system is designed for dust, but filters still need regular service when you cut dry.

Cutting concrete and stone dry throws crystalline silica dust, which is a serious lung hazard and regulated by OSHA. The K770 has a water kit; hook up a hose or a pressurized tank and cut wet whenever you are on masonry. Wet cutting also keeps diamond blades cooler and longer lived.
Wear eye protection, hearing protection, gloves and a respirator suited to the task. Keep the blade guard set so sparks and slurry go away from you, and stand to the side of the cutting line.
Slurry from wet cutting is slick and can stain. Plan where the water will run, protect nearby finishes and clean up before the slurry dries.

The typical Husqvarna K770 price is around the figure shown, usually without a blade. Budget for blades, a spare air filter and a water tank if you will not always have a hose. Run fresh 50:1 mix, clean the filters often, and check the drive belt tension when the cutter feels like it is slipping in the cut.
Compare it with other jobsite gear in our blowers and other equipment section. Anyone running a power cutter should be trained on kickback and pull-in, which work differently from a chainsaw.

faq.q: What blade size does the Husqvarna K770 use?
faq.a: It runs 12 in. or 14 in. blades. A 14 in. blade gives about 5 in. of cutting depth.

faq.q: Can the K770 cut steel?
faq.a: Yes, with a blade rated for steel. Match the blade to the material and the saw's RPM.

faq.q: Do I need to cut wet with the K770?
faq.a: On concrete, stone and masonry, cutting wet is the best way to control silica dust. Use the water kit and wear proper respiratory protection.

tagline: Tough, long-wearing trimmer line for crews who clean up heavy growth after the tree work.
summary: Husqvarna Titanium Force trimmer line is a reinforced string built to last longer against fences, rock and woody stems. The Titanium X-Pro grade is the pick when standard line keeps snapping on heavy cleanup.
highlights: Reinforced titanium-additive line for longer wear
Holds up against fence posts, rock and curbs
Shaped profile for clean cutting of thick grass and weeds

Spool and donut sizes for shop and truck

body.h: Why crews run titanium weed eater string
p: A tree job is not always finished when the last log is loaded. Overgrown fence lines, stumps surrounded by weeds and edges chewed up by the chipper all need a trimmer, and cheap line breaks the moment it touches chain link or stone. Husqvarna titanium x pro line is made to keep cutting through that kind of abuse, which means fewer stops to bump or rewind the head.
Husqvarna titanium force string trimmer line uses a reinforced polymer blend. The result is line that resists welding together on the spool in hot weather and wears down more slowly at the tip.

The titanium weed eater string label refers to the reinforcing material in the blend, not a metal wire. It is still a polymer line that is safe to use in normal trimmer heads, but it is stiffer and tougher than basic line.

Always use the diameter your trimmer head is designed for. Thicker line cuts heavier growth but needs more engine power and may not fit small heads. Light-duty trimmers do best with smaller line; professional gas trimmers and brushcutters can run thicker line for weeds, cane and light brush.
If your head's eyelets show a maximum size, stay within it. Line that is too heavy loads the engine, overheats the clutch and wears the head faster. Line that is too light snaps constantly.

Profile matters too. Shaped line has edges that slice grass and weeds rather than tearing them, which leaves a cleaner finish and takes a little less power. Round line is quieter and tends to last longer against hard edges, so pick based on where you spend most of your time.

Wind line tight and even onto the spool, in the direction marked on the head, and do not overfill. A loose or crossed wind causes jams. Cut a fresh end at an angle so it feeds cleanly through the eyelet.

Store spare line out of direct sun. Some crews soak line in water overnight before loading it to keep it supple, which can help in very dry, hot climates. Keep the spool bagged so it does not pick up grit in the truck.

Buy line in the size of package that suits your crew. A small donut is fine for a single trimmer on the truck, while a large spool in the shop is cheaper per foot if you run several machines and reload often.

Trimmers throw rock, glass and wood chips hard. Wear eye protection, hearing protection and long pants, and keep bystanders and other crew well back. Use the guard that came with your trimmer. Compare with Husqvarna TrimForce trimmer line if you want a more economical everyday option, and browse our landscaper tools for heads and accessories.
Before trimming around a finished tree job, walk the area and pick up loose wood, wire and stones. A trimmer hitting a stray piece of hardware can throw it a long way.

faq.q: Is Husqvarna Titanium Force line worth the extra cost?
faq.a: For crews trimming around fences, rock and woody stems, longer-lasting line usually saves time and line overall.

faq.q: What size trimmer line should I buy?
faq.a: Use the diameter your trimmer head is rated for. Check the head or the owner's manual.

faq.q: Will this line fit non-Husqvarna trimmers?
faq.a: Yes, as long as the diameter matches what your trimmer head accepts.

title: Husqvarna Trimmer Line: TrimForce for Everyday Trimming
h1: Husqvarna Trimmer Line: TrimForce

Feeds cleanly from bump and fixed-line heads
Available in common diameters
